cards.explanation: The answer is False. Matthew says the darkness came "…over all the land." Golgotha is only one spot in it. It stayed from the sixth hour until the ninth hour. Imagine, friends, stepping outside in the middle of the day and finding the whole sky dark.

The answer is Elijah. Some of those standing there heard Jesus cry "Eli, Eli" and said, "He is calling Elijah." Elijah was a prophet from long ago (1 Kings 18:36). They heard a cry in the darkness, friends, and that's the name they landed on.

The answer is that he holds it up for Jesus to drink. One of the people standing there quickly ran and brought a sponge. He filled it with sour wine, put it on a reed, and held it up for Jesus to drink. Look at how fast he moves, friends. Matthew says he quickly ran.

The answer is "Leave Him alone." The others said, "Leave Him alone." Then they added, "Let us see if Elijah comes to save Him." So one man brings the sponge and the others say that. I think that's a lot of opinions for one cross, friends.

The answer is quakes. Matthew says, "The earth quaked, and the rocks were split." That happened at the moment Jesus yielded up His spirit. This was no little wobble on the counter, friends. Even the rocks split.

The answer is that they are raised. Matthew says the tombs broke open, and the bodies of many saints who had fallen asleep were raised. "Saints" here means God's people who had died, friends. Matthew tells us that plainly and goes on with the story.

The answer is True. Matthew says that after Jesus' resurrection, when they had come out of the tombs, they entered the holy city and appeared to many people. Notice, friends, that the verse puts it after His resurrection. Matthew tells it just that way.

The answer is terrified. Matthew says the centurion and those with him were terrified when they saw the earthquake and all that had happened. These men were guarding Jesus, and I bet a shaking earth was the last thing they expected. I think I'd have dropped my whole tray of cookies, friends.

The answer is "Truly this was the Son of God." The centurion and those with him said exactly that. Matthew doesn't say why they said it, friends, only that they saw the earthquake and all that had happened. These were the men guarding Jesus, and that's what came out of them.

The answer is to minister to Him. Matthew says the women had followed Jesus from Galilee to minister to Him. They came all the way from Galilee to serve Him, friends, and they're still there watching. I think that tells you something about them.
